newsitem.title: UK: Greece gets Moody's upgrade after fiscal progress.
newsitem.headline: Greece gets Moody's upgrade after fiscal progress.

text.p: Greece's effort to improve state finances and align its economic performance with its richer European Union partners was rewarded on Monday with a credit ratings upgrade by Moody's Investors Service.

Moody's said it raised the sovereign ceilings for long-term foreign-currency bonds and bank deposits of Greece to Baa1 from Baa3, while the sovereign ceiling for short-term notes and deposits was raised to Prime 2 from Prime 3.

Moody's said the upgrades were triggered by improvement in fiscal balances in the past few years and the stronger political resolve to continue with policies consistent with European Union convergence.
"On the macroeconomic front, the economy has began expanding thanks to the robust growth of investment, both private and public," Moody's said in a statement.

It said industrial production has picked up and manufacturing employment has stopped falling. Inflation has been reduced to single digit levels, for the first time in two decades, and confidence has been established in the drachma.
Structural weaknesses persist, however, particularly regarding the current account of the balance of payments, Moody's said.

"Budgetary adjustments have been made so far mostly on the revenue side," Moody's said. "The reduction in the 1997 budget deficit is achieved through a combination of revenue enhancing measures -- including the abolition of some tax benefits and allowances and some new taxes-- as well as some expenditure controlling measures."
Last month Greece unveiled a 1997 austerity budget, aimed at putting the EU's poorest country on a better footing to join a single European currency.
